gi8_golan.topic: Golan Heights 1967-2023: 1981 law, UNSC 497, US 2019 recognition, Colombia 2026, 2016 and 2021 statements, 1994-2000 talks

claims.text: The Knesset passed the Golan Heights Law on 14 December 1981 by 63 votes to 21; its key clause: 'The Law, jurisdiction and administration of the State will take effect in the Golan Heights'; Begin told the Knesset Israel could not wait indefinitely for a Syrian signal of willingness to negotiate and cited historical, security and 'moral-political' reasons; Time attributed it to coalition pressure, Likud's 1981 manifesto, the failed Habib mission and Syria's opposition to the Fahd Plan.

The US temporarily suspended the November 1981 strategic cooperation agreement; the State Department said the law was passed without consulting Washington; Reagan said it 'increased the difficulty of seeking peace'.

Druze of the Golan began a three-day general strike on 17 December 1981, wrote to Begin that they were Syrian Arabs and would resist forced citizenship; the 1982 general strike lasted about five months and led to an Israeli blockade of Druze towns.

UNSC Resolution 497, adopted unanimously (15-0-0) on 17 December 1981 at the 2319th meeting: Israel's decision to impose its laws, jurisdiction and administration on the occupied Syrian Golan Heights is 'null and void and without international legal effect'; demands Israel rescind it; Fourth Geneva Convention continues to apply; Council to meet 'not later than 5 January 1982' if Israel did not comply.

On 20 January 1982 the US vetoed a follow-up draft calling for international action against Israel under Chapter VII; on 5 February 1982 a General Assembly emergency special session adopted 86-21 a resolution calling for a boycott of Israel, the US and many Western states voting against.

Proclamation 9852, 25 March 2019: 'the United States recognizes that the Golan Heights are part of the State of Israel'; rationale: Israel 'took control of the Golan Heights in 1967 to safeguard its security from external threats', and 'aggressive acts by Iran and terrorist groups, including Hizballah, in southern Syria'.

Trump tweeted on 21 March 2019 it was time to recognise Israel's 'Sovereignty over the Golan Heights'; Syria called it a 'blatant attack' on its sovereignty; the EU, UK, Germany, France, the Arab League rejected it; Guterres said the Golan's status had not changed; Israel announced 'Trump Heights' on 16 June 2019; the recognition continued under Biden.

Colombia's Foreign Ministry announced on Monday 10 August 2026, days after President Abelardo de la Espriella took office (7 August), that it 'recognises Israeli sovereignty over this territory'; Colombia became the second country after the US; Saar called it 'historic'; Netanyahu thanked Colombia; Syria lodged a UN complaint on 12 August ('protest, condemnation and categorical rejection'); Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Egypt, Jordan, Oman and Turkey condemned it; the UN still considers the Golan Syrian.
At the first official cabinet meeting held on the Golan, 17 April 2016, Netanyahu: 'The Golan Heights will forever remain in Israel's hands. Israel will never come down from the Golan Heights.'

On 26 December 2021 the Bennett cabinet, meeting on the Golan, unanimously approved a 1 billion shekel (about $320m) plan including two new communities, Asif and Matar; Bennett: 'our goal today is to double the population of the Golan Heights'; the Golan population was about 53,000, roughly half Israeli settlers and half Syrian Druze; Syria said it 'reject[s] the annexation decision and the policy of seizing lands by force'.

In 1994 Rabin made secret contacts with Damascus and proposed a partial withdrawal over about three years within a comprehensive peace, subject to a referendum; Syria insisted on complete withdrawal; Shepherdstown talks 3-11 January 2000 failed; on 26 March 2000 in Geneva Asad rejected Barak's proposal, carried by Clinton, because it left Israel sovereignty over a strip north of Lake Tiberias, 'effectively the end of the negotiations'.

gi8_sinai.topic: Egypt and Sinai: 1979 treaty text, 1982 completion, Taba 1988-89

claims.text: Egypt-Israel treaty, 26 March 1979, Art. I(2): 'Israel will withdraw all its armed forces and civilians from the Sinai'; Art. II: boundary is the recognized line between Egypt and the former mandated territory of Palestine, 'without prejudice to the issue of the status of the Gaza Strip', recognized 'as inviolable'; Annex I: interim withdrawal within nine months of ratification, final withdrawal 'not later than three years'; witnessed by Carter.

Taba (about 250 acres on the Gulf of Aqaba): in January 1982 Israeli negotiators argued it should stay in Israel, citing ambiguities in the 1906 border description; Israel built two hotels there; cabinet accepted arbitration 13 January 1986 under Art. 7 of the treaty; panel ruled for Egypt on 29 September 1988; Israel evacuated Taba on 15 March 1989.

gi8_jordan.topic: Jordan: 1994 treaty, Baqura/Ghamr 2019, 'Jordan is Palestine', Smotrich 2023 map and MFA reaffirmation, King Abdullah 'alternative homeland'

claims.text: Israel-Jordan treaty, 26 October 1994: Art. 2 the parties 'recognise and will respect each other's sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence'; Art. 3 boundary 'delimited with reference to the boundary definition under the Mandate', the 'permanent, secure and recognised international boundary', 'without prejudice to the status of any territories that came under Israeli military government control in 1967'; Art. 3(8) Naharayim/Baqura 'under Jordanian sovereignty, with Israeli private ownership rights'; Art. 9(2) Israel respects 'the present special role of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan in Muslim Holy shrines in Jerusalem'.

Signed at the Arava crossing by Rabin and Majali, Clinton present; Knesset approved 92-3; Israel recognised Jordanian sovereignty over Naharayim/Baqura and Tzofar/Ghamr; Annex I let Jordan decline to renew the leases after 25 years with a year's notice; Jordan gave notice in October 2018; Israel to supply 50 million cubic metres of water a year.

10 November 2019: King Abdullah told parliament of 'the expiration of the Peace Treaty annexes on Ghamr and al-Baqura' and Jordan's 'full sovereignty'; Israel's Foreign Ministry said Israel 'regrets Jordan's decision to terminate the annexes'; Baqura captured by Israel in 1950, Ghamr in 1967; Israeli farmers allowed to harvest that season.

Pipes and Garfinkle (Commentary, Oct 1988) quote Shamir in 1982: 'That homeland is Trans-Jordan, or Eastern Palestine'; say the argument 'has long underlain the policy of the Likud bloc'; tie Sharon to the idea (as minister he encouraged West Bank and Gaza Arabs to cross the river) without a direct quote; quote King Hussein in 1981 'Jordan is Palestine and Palestine is Jordan' and on 31 July 1988 'Jordan is not Palestine'; the authors call the idea 'historically wrong' and its implementation 'extremely dangerous'.

Lynch (MERIP 2004): Sharon and the Likud right held that a Palestinian state already existed in Jordan ('Jordan is Palestine'); Sharon reportedly favoured overthrowing King Hussein; Sharon abstained in the Knesset vote on the 1994 treaty; in March 2004 King Abdullah reportedly warned Sharon not to encourage talk of a 'Jordan option'.
King Abdullah II, 7 January 2004, Amman: the substitute-country issue 'is being raised from time to time by different parties' and 'Jordan will never be an alternative homeland to anybody'.

Smotrich spoke in Paris at a memorial for a far-right activist (Axios: 'Sunday, March 20'; Sunday was 19 March 2023) at a podium bearing a 'Greater Israel' map including Jordan and the West Bank; said Palestinians are 'an invention' and 'There is no such thing as a Palestinian people'; Jordan summoned Israel's ambassador, accused him of violating the treaty and condemned 'racist, inciting and extremist statements'.

Israel's Foreign Ministry, 20 March 2023: 'Israel is committed to the 1994 peace agreement with Jordan. There has been no change in the position of the State of Israel, which recognizes the territorial integrity of the Hashemite Kingdom'; Hanegbi told Safadi Israel is committed to the treaty; Smotrich had not commented.
